title: fix(service-automation): a failing parallel keeps every branch's steps in the run log
body:
Fixes #23928

Clause-②: no

## What an operator now sees on a failed `parallel` run

The run's step log lists every branch's steps under the block's own `failure` step. Each is tagged `parentNodeId`, `regionKind: 'parallel-branch'` and its `branch` index: a branch that completed, with its `success` step, and the failing branch's steps up to and including the one that failed, with its error. The run summary counts what those steps did. On the card's fan-out (branch 0 an inbox `notify`, branch 1 an `http` POST failing with `fetch failed`) the run now reads `selected: 1, acted: 1, failed: 2`. Before, it read `acted: 0` beside a notification that had already been delivered, and `acted: 0` on a failed run reads as "nothing happened, safe to re-run".

## The change: `builtin/parallel-node.ts`, `execute`

- Each branch runs `engine.runRegion(...)` with its **own** `partialSteps` sink. A failing branch's tagged region steps land in its sink before `runRegion` rethrows, and a completed branch returns its steps instead. So each step is collected exactly once, in branch declaration order, the order the success path already used.
- Each branch's promise is wrapped so it never rejects, and its rejection is recorded in settle order. The block therefore reports its failure **once every branch has settled**, so a sibling that finishes after another branch failed keeps its step too. The failure reported is the first one in settle order, which is the one `Promise.all` rejected with before, so the error text is unchanged.
- A branch failure is still **returned** as `{ success: false, error }`, now with `childSteps`. A region-suspension refusal is still **re-thrown** unchanged, now carrying the branch steps through `attachPartialSteps`.

No `engine.ts` change. The engine already folds a returned failure's `childSteps` right behind the container's own step (`engine.ts:11812`, the arm `try_catch` uses), and a thrown error's partial steps the same way (`engine.ts:11689`).

## Why return for a branch failure, and throw only for the refusal

The deciding constraint is `partial-steps.ts:40-47`: a step-record fix must not move accept/reject behaviour, and the returned and thrown failure paths route differently. `loop` used to throw, so it kept throwing and carried its steps on the error (`loop-node.ts:151-159`). `parallel` already **returned** its branch failure (`parallel-node.ts:106` at base). The same rule points the other way here: keep returning, and put `childSteps` on the result. A switch to a throw would move the block's step code from `NODE_FAILURE` to `EXECUTION_ERROR`, change `$error`'s shape and rewrite the run's error text, the same costs `partial-steps.ts` names. The region-suspension refusal was already thrown (`parallel-node.ts:104` at base) so that a `fault` edge cannot route it. It keeps the throw and gets `attachPartialSteps`, which leaves the error's identity, message and refusal marking untouched. That is `loop`'s mechanism, on the one path where `parallel` already threw.

## Tests

- **Red at base, 10 of 10.** `parallel-node.test.ts` (8 new pins) and the new `parallel-failed-branch-steps.integration.test.ts` (2 pins), run on commit 836fb42e33 (pins only, source at base 7277c07f68): `Tests 10 failed | 7 passed (17)`. Readings: `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'notify_owner@par/0:success', ... ]` (no branch steps), `expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 1` (acted), `expected [ 'par', 'recover' ] to deeply equal [ 'par', 'notify_owner', 'x', ... ]` (the fault edge routes at base but the branch steps are missing), and `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'slow' ]` (at base the failed run returned before the slow sibling had even delivered).
- **Green with the fix:** the same two files give `Tests 17 passed (17)`. The full package suite (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation test`) gives `Test Files 188 passed (188)`, `Tests 2519 passed (2519)`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation typecheck` exits 0: `tsc --noEmit`, then `check:test-typecheck: OK ... 0 file(s) / 0 error(s)`.
- **Real engine:** `parallel-failed-branch-steps.integration.test.ts` runs the real `notify` node on a real inline `MessagingService` with a recording `inbox` channel, and the real `http` node with the global `fetch` rejecting `TypeError('fetch failed')`, the card's failure. It asserts the step log carries `notify_owner` `success` on branch 0 and `slack_post` `failure` with its error on branch 1, and that the live result and the persisted run row both read `selected: 1, acted: 1`, `unmeasured: 1` (the failed POST) and `failed: 2`. The other pins cover: the failing branch's steps up to and including its failure, a sibling that settles after the failure, the reverse control (no effect, `acted: 0`), a `fault` edge routing as before with the branch steps between the block and its handler, the refused pause (`failed` stays 1), and `loop { parallel }` folding each step exactly once.
- **Ablation** through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (WRAP mode: anchor hit x1 to x0, blob changed, restore proven blob == HEAD `47a3dfb296d0` and `git diff HEAD` empty, each leg):
  - Leg 1 drops `childSteps` from the returned failure (blob to `861c8de3a97f`): `Tests 9 failed | 8 passed (17)`. Every returned-failure pin goes red, including both integration pins; the pause pin stays green because it rides the other limb.
  - Leg 2 reverts the refusal rethrow to a bare `throw err;` (blob to `d99181112ccd`), run with `region-durable-suspension-refusal.test.ts` too: `Tests 1 failed | 24 passed (25)`. Only the pause pin goes red (`expected [] to include 'notify_owner@par/0:success'`); the existing region-refusal suite stays green both ways.
  - The join-before-failure limb has no single-line ablation. Its red reading is the base run above (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'slow' ]`).

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at 4c26145a93 (this head, after merging `origin/main` 161aee1047, which touched only `packages/cli` and `driver-turso`): 63 commands. 62 exited 0, exit captured before any pipe. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — this gate reads built output, and some package has no dist/`. That means it measured nothing here (it needs the whole-workspace build), so it is NOT MEASURED locally and left to CI's `Lint & Repo Gates`. `--ran` reconciliation: `63 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 1 UNRUN` (that one), plus the package test and typecheck recorded outside the derivation.

`Clause-②: no`: the diff changes no exported declaration. `registerParallelNode`'s signature is untouched and everything else is inside `execute`. The built declaration closure was not diffed against base.

## Acceptance notes

- Timing: a failed block now reports its failure (and a `fault` handler starts) once every branch has settled, not at the first rejection. A slow sibling therefore delays the handler, bounded by its nodes' own timeouts. This is the documented implicit join. Before, a sibling could finish its effect after the run had already recorded the failure.
- Stale comments in `engine.ts`, which this PR does not touch (another PR holds it): the returned-failure fold says `try_catch` "is still the only" producer of `childSteps` on a failing result, and `runRegion`'s doc says callers that pass no sink are "`loop`, `parallel`". Both now pass one. Carrier: none.
- Observation, preserved on purpose: when one branch fails at runtime FIRST and another later raises a region-suspension refusal, the block returns the first (routable) failure, exactly as `Promise.all` chose before. Only the first failure in settle order is acted on, so routing does not move. Read from source and not measured through a public door, so not filed. Carrier: none.
- The Studio Runs panel (objectui) was not driven. The card measured it rendering no branch rows under a failed `parallel`. Whether it now renders them is not measured here.
